rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those astray from their Lord's path are the truly mad; the guided are those who attain complete intellect.
rows.anchor: إن ربك هو أعلم بمن ضل عن سبيله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guided are the successful, possessing complete intellect.
rows.anchor: { وهو أعلم بالمهتدين } الفائزين بكمال العقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition urges firm resolve to oppose the deniers.
rows.anchor: { فلا تطع المكذبين } تهييج للتصميم على معاصاتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deniers want the Prophet to soften toward them by ceasing to forbid associating partners with God.
rows.anchor: تلاينهم بأن تدع نهيهم عن الشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another form of the requested compromise would be to agree with the deniers in shirk on some occasions.
rows.anchor: أو توافقهم فيه أحيانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They would reciprocate by softening their attacks and agreeing to compromise.
rows.anchor: فيلاينونك بترك الطعن والموافقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fa may coordinate: they desire and defer their own compromise until the Prophet compromises first.
rows.anchor: والفاء للعطف أي ودوا التداهن وتمنوه لكنهم أخروا ادهانهم حتى تدهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the fa gives the result: if the Prophet compromised, they would then reciprocate.
rows.anchor: أو للسببية أي { ودوا لو تدهن } فهم يدهنون حينئذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, they desire the Prophet's compromise and already soften their stance in expectation of it.
rows.anchor: أو ودوا ادهانك فهم الآن يدهنون طمعا فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some codices read “فيدهنوا,” treating the verb as the response to the wish.
rows.anchor: وفي بعض المصاحف «فيدهنوا» على أنه جواب التمني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A ḥallāf is someone who swears frequently, whether truthfully or falsely.
rows.anchor: حلاف } كثير الحلف في الحق والباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mahīn means contemptible in judgment, from a root meaning lowliness.
rows.anchor: مهين } حقير الرأي من المهانة وهي الحقارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A zaʿīm is a guarantor who claims and substantiates the proposed judgment.
rows.anchor: بذلك الحكم قائم يدعيه ويصححه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they claim partners support their judgment, they should produce them; even blind imitation would require such partners to exist.
rows.anchor: { فليأتوا بشركائهم إن كانوا صدقين } في دعواهم إذ لا أقل من التقليد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The questions sequentially rule out every possible support: reason, transmitted proof, promise, then mere imitation, corresponding to ranks of inquiry.
rows.anchor: على الترتيب تنبيها على مراتب النظر وتزييفا لما لا سند له

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The “partners” are idols whom the deniers imagine will make them equal to believers in the afterlife; God having denied that He would do so, the verse denies that partners could.
rows.anchor: وقيل المعنى { أم لهم شركاء } يعني الأصنام يجعلونهم مثل المؤمنين في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Uncovering a ساق depicts an intensely difficult affair; the image originates in women hitching up their skirts while fleeing.
rows.anchor: يوم يشتد الأمر ويصعب الخطب

rows.speaker: حاتم
rows.claim: Hatim's battle poem uses uncovering the ساق as an image for war's severe onset.
rows.anchor: قال حاتم. أخو الحرب إن عضت به الحرب عضها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the phrase means the root and reality of the matter will be uncovered until it becomes visible, by analogy with a tree's or person's trunk.
rows.anchor: أو يوم يكشف عن أصل الأمر وحقيقته بحيث يصير عيانا مستعار من ساق الشجر وساق الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite form of ساق conveys awe or magnification.
rows.anchor: وتنكيره للتهويل أو للتعظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb is also read with tāʾ, in active or passive form, with the Hour or the circumstance as its subject.
rows.anchor: وقرىء «تكشف» و «تكشف» بالتاء على بناء الفاعل أو المفعول والفعل للساعة أو الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the scene is Judgment Day, the call rebukes them for neglecting prostration; if it is the moment of death, it calls them to prayers at their appointed times.
rows.anchor: توبيخا على تركهم السجود إن كان اليوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They cannot prostrate because its time has passed or their ability has disappeared.
rows.anchor: لذهاب وقته أو زوال القدرة عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humiliation overtakes them while their eyes are downcast.
rows.anchor: { خشعة أبصرهم ترهقهم ذلة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They had been called to prostrate in worldly life or while they were healthy.
rows.anchor: في الدنيا أو زمان الصحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In life they had the ability to prostrate and were free of impediments.
rows.anchor: متمكنون منه مزاحو العلل فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God tells the Prophet to leave those rejecting the whole revelation to Him; He will suffice against them.
rows.anchor: كله إلي فإني أكفيكه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gradually draws them nearer to punishment through respite, continued health, and increasing blessings, without their recognizing the process.
rows.anchor: سندنيهم من العذاب درجة درجة بالإمهال وإدامة الصحة وازدياد النعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They mistake this gradual enticement for preference over the believers.
rows.anchor: لأنهم حسبوه تفضيلا لهم على المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the blessings a “plot” is apt because they outwardly resemble one; God's plot cannot be repelled.
rows.anchor: سمي إنعامه استدراجا بالكيد لأنه في صورته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are not turning away because the Prophet charges them for guidance and burdens them with payment.
rows.anchor: على الإرشاد. { فهم من مغرم } من غرامة. { مثقلون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unseen may mean the Preserved Tablet or hidden matters.
rows.anchor: اللوح أو المغيبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They supposedly write judgments from the unseen and thereby dispense with the Prophet's knowledge.
rows.anchor: منه ما يحكمون به ويستغنون به عن علمك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ṭāghiya may be an overwhelmingly severe event, either the blast or the quake, because they denied the Calamity.
rows.anchor: بالواقعة المجاوزة للحد في الشدة وهي الصيحة، أو الرجفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it is the verbal noun for their transgression through denial and other acts; this reading as a verbal noun does not agree grammatically with the following account of ʿĀd.
rows.anchor: أو بسبب طغيانهم بالتكذيب وغيره على أنها مصدر كالعاقبة وهو لا يطابق قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣarṣar means a wind of intense sound or intense cold, from roots denoting loudness or cold.
rows.anchor: أي شديدة الصوت أو البرد من الصر أو الصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wind was fiercely violent, as though it defied its keepers' control or defied ʿĀd's efforts to repel it.
rows.anchor: شديدة العصف كأنها عتت على خزانها فلم يستطيعوا ضبطها، أو على { عاد } فلم يقدروا على ردها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God subjected the wind to them by His power; this may be a new clause or an adjective that rejects an astrological explanation.
rows.anchor: هو استئناف أو صفة جيء به لنفي ما يتوهم من أنها كانت من اتصالات فلكية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if the wind had astral connections, God would still be its determiner and cause.
rows.anchor: إذ لو كانت لكان هو المقدر لها والمسبب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥusūman may mean successive days, by analogy with repeatedly cauterizing an animal.
rows.anchor: متتابعات جمع حاسم من حسمت الدابة إذا تابعت بين كيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, they were ill-omened days that cut off every good, or days that severed the people's descendants.
rows.anchor: أو نحسات حسمت كل خير واستأصلته، أو قاطعات قطعت دابرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word may be an accusative of cause meaning “severely,” or an absolute verbal noun for an implied verb, used circumstantially; the fatḥa reading supports the latter.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون مصدرا منتصبا على العلة بمعنى قطعا، أو المصدر لفعله المقدر حالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The days were the Days of the Old Woman, from Wednesday morning through the following Wednesday sunset.
rows.anchor: وهي كانت أيام العجوز من صبيحة أربعاء إلى غروب الأربعاء الآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The days were called “the old woman's” either because they ended winter or because an old woman of ʿĀd was pulled from her hiding place by the wind on the eighth day and killed.
rows.anchor: وإنما سميت عجوزا لأنها عجز الشتاء، أو لأن عجوزا من عاد توارت في سرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address imagines the listener present among them or in the wind's path; ṣarʿā means dead, and khāwiya means decayed inside.
rows.anchor: إن كنت حاضرهم { فيها } في مهابها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dead are compared to the bases of palm trees, hollowed and decayed within.
rows.anchor: { كأنهم أعجاز نخل } أصول نخل. { خاوية } متأكلة الأجواف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase can mean any remnant, any surviving person, or survival itself.
rows.anchor: من بقية أو نفس باقية، أو بقاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the standard reading, “before him” means those who preceded Pharaoh.
rows.anchor: ومن تقدمه

rows.speaker: البصريان والكسائي
rows.claim: The Basran readers and al-Kisāʾī read “ومن قبله,” meaning those with or around Pharaoh; “ومن معه” is also transmitted as support.
rows.anchor: وقرأ البصريان والكسائي { ومن قبله } أي ومن عنده من أتباعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “overturned cities” are the people of Lot's towns.
rows.anchor: قرى قوم لوط والمراد أهلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-khāṭiʾa may mean error, a sinful act, or deeds characterized by error.
rows.anchor: بالخطأ أو بالفعلة، أو الأفعال ذات الخطأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each community disobeyed its own messenger.
rows.anchor: أي فعصت كل أمة رسولها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seizure exceeded ordinary severity in proportion to the increased ugliness of their deeds.
rows.anchor: زائدة في الشدة زيادة أعمالهم في القبح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The floodwater exceeded its normal limit or overwhelmed its keepers; it occurred in Noah's Flood and supports the preceding account.
rows.anchor: جاوز حده المعتاد، أو طغى على خزانه وذلك في الطوفان وهو يؤيد من قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God carried the audience's ancestors, with the audience still in their loins.
rows.anchor: أي آباءكم وأنتم في أصلابهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vessel is Noah's Ark.
rows.anchor: في سفينة نوح عليه الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The remembered event is the rescue of believers and drowning of unbelievers; it teaches the Maker's power, wisdom, dominance, and mercy.
rows.anchor: لنجعل الفعلة وهي إنجاء المؤمنين وإغراق الكافرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To “retain” it is to preserve and remember it within oneself; īʿāʾ is preserving something outside oneself.
rows.anchor: والوعي أن تحفظ الشيء في نفسك والإيعاء أن تحفظه في غيرك

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr reads the word with a quiescent ʿayn, analogizing its form to “katif.”
rows.anchor: وعن ابن كثير «تعيها» بسكون العين تشبيها بكتف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A receptive ear retains what should be remembered, shared, reflected on, and acted upon; the indefinite form highlights how few such people can help save multitudes and perpetuate their descendants.
rows.anchor: من شأنها أن تحفظ ما يجب حفظه بتذكره وإشاعته والتفكر فيه

rows.speaker: نافع
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ reads “أذن” with a lightened dhāl.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع «أذن» بالتخفيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeing the ugliness of his deeds and the bad outcome leads the recipient of the book in his left hand to regret it.
rows.anchor: لما يرى من قبح العمل وسوء العاقبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He wishes he had never received his record.
rows.anchor: يليتنى لم أوت كتبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He wishes his previous death had ended everything and he had not been resurrected.
rows.anchor: القاطعة لأمري فلم أبعث بعدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, he wishes his present condition were death, since it has proved worse than death.
rows.anchor: لأنه صادفها أمر من الموت فتمناه عندها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, he wishes worldly life had been death, so that he had never lived in it.
rows.anchor: أو يا ليت حياة الدنيا كانت الموتة ولم أخلق فيها حيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “My wealth” includes property and followers; mā may be a negation with an omitted object, or an interrogative object of “benefit,” making a denial.
rows.anchor: مالي من المال والتبع وما نفى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sulṭānihi may mean his rule and power over people or the argument he used in worldly life.
rows.anchor: ملكي وتسلطي على الناس، أو حجتي التي كنت أحتج بها في الدنيا

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: Ḥamza drops both final hāʾs in connected reading; the other readers retain them in both connected and paused forms.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة «عني» «مالي» «عني سلطاني» بحذف الهاءين في الوصل والباقون بإثباتها في الحالين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God addresses the keepers of the Fire, commanding them to seize the condemned person.
rows.anchor: يقوله الله تعالى لخزنة النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are to shackle him.
rows.anchor: يقوله الله تعالى لخزنة النار. { فغلوه }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are to roast him only in the greatest fire, fitting because he exalted himself over people.
rows.anchor: وهي النار العظمى لأنه كان يتعظم على الناس

words: ثم في سلسلة ذرعها سبعون ذراعا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The chain is extremely long; they put it over his body while he is trapped among its links and unable to move.
rows.anchor: فأدخلوه فيها بأن تلقوها على جسده وهو فيما بينها مرهق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Putting the Fire and then the chain first signals particularity and draws attention to the kinds of torment; thumma marks their differing severity.
rows.anchor: وتقديم ال { سلسلة } كتقديم { الجحيم } للدلالة على التخصيص والاهتمام بذكر أنواع ما يعذب به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His faṣīla is the clan from whom he separated.
rows.anchor: وعشيرته الذين فصل عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His clan shelters him through kinship or in times of hardship.
rows.anchor: تضمه في النسب أو عند الشدائد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people on earth may mean both accountable kinds, humans and jinn, or all creatures.
rows.anchor: من الثقلين أو الخلائق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Then it would save him” coordinates with “ransom”; thumma conveys how far-fetched such salvation is.
rows.anchor: عطف على { يفتدي } أي ثم ينجيه الافتداء و { ثم } للاستبعاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebuke dissuades the criminal from wishing for ransom and declares that ransom will not save him.
rows.anchor: ردع للمجرم عن الودادة ودلالة على أن الافتداء لا ينجيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to the Fire, or is an indefinite pronoun explained by laẓā; alternatively it refers to the affair, with laẓā as subject.
rows.anchor: الضمير للنار أو مبهم يفسره { لظى } وهو خبر أو بدل أو للقصة و { لظى } مبتدأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Laẓā means a pure flame; it may instead be a name for the Fire derived from the word for flame.
rows.anchor: وهو اللهب الخالص وقيل علم للنار منقول من اللظى بمعنى اللهب

rows.speaker: حفص عن عاصم
rows.claim: Ḥafṣ, from ʿĀṣim, reads nazzāʿatan in the accusative, as specification or as an emphatic or transferred circumstantial.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حفص عن عاصم { نزاعة } بالنصب على الاختصاص أو الحال المؤكدة أو المتنقلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If laẓā means blazing, nazzāʿa describes the Fire as stripping away appendages; shawa may mean extremities or the skin of the skull.
rows.anchor: على أن { لظى } بمعنى متلظية والشوى والأطراف أو جمع شواة وهي جلدة الرأس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Fire draws in and brings near those who flee from it, metaphorically described as calling them.
rows.anchor: تجذب وتحضر كقول ذي الرمة

rows.speaker: ذي الرمة
rows.claim: Dhu al-Rummah's verse uses tadʿū for drawing something toward oneself, supporting this sense.
rows.anchor:
كقول ذي الرمة:
تدعو أنفه الريب

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, the Fire calls its keepers.
rows.anchor: وقيل تدعو زبانيتها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, “calls” means destroys, as in the idiom “God called him” meaning that God destroyed him.
rows.anchor: وقيل تدعو تهلك من قولهم دعاه الله إذا أهلكه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ones who turn away have turned from truth and obedience.
rows.anchor: عن الحق { وتولى } عن الطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūrat al-Jinn is Meccan and has twenty-eight verses.
rows.anchor: مكية، وآيها ثمان وعشرون آية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb is also read “أحي” or in its original form “وحي”; the hamza replaces wāw because of its ḍamma.
rows.anchor: وقرىء «أحي» وأصله وحى من وحى إليه فقلبت الواو همزة لضمتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause “that a group of jinn listened” is the subject of the verb “was revealed.”
rows.anchor: وفاعله: { أنه استمع نفر من الجن }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nafar denotes a group of between three and ten.
rows.anchor: والنفر ما بين الثلاثة إلى العشرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jinn are intelligent, hidden beings, predominantly fiery or airy; alternatives identify them as separate spirits or human souls separated from bodies.
rows.anchor: وقيل نوع من الأرواح المجردة وقيل نفوس بشرية مفارقة عن أبدانها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet did not see the jinn or recite directly to them; they happened to hear one of his recitations, and God informed him of it.
rows.anchor: وفيه دلالة على أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام ما رآهم ولم يقرأ عليهم وإنما اتفق حضورهم في بعض أوقات قراءته فسمعوها فأخبر الله به رسوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The jinn spoke after returning to their people.
rows.anchor: لما رجعوا إلى قومهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurʾān here means a book.
rows.anchor: قرآنا } كتابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾān is wondrous and unlike human speech in the beauty of its arrangement and precision of meaning; the verbal noun is used adjectivally for emphasis.
rows.anchor: بديعا مباينا لكلام الناس في حسن نظمه ودقة معناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The provision tests whether they are grateful for it.
rows.anchor: لنختبرهم كيف يشكرونه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, had the jinn remained on their old path instead of embracing Islam after hearing the Qurʾān, provision would have been expanded to lure them into ingratitude and punishment.
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه أن لو استقام الجن على طريقتهم القديمة ولم يسلموا باستماع القرآن لوسعنا عليهم الرزق مستدرجين لهم لنوقعهم في الفتنة ونعذبهم في كفرانهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “remembrance of his Lord” may mean worship, admonition, or revelation.
rows.anchor: عن عبادته أو موعظته أو وحيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaslukhu means “He enters him into it.”
rows.anchor: { يسلكه } يدخله وقرأ غير الكوفيين بالنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readers other than the Kufans read the verb with nūn.
rows.anchor: وقرأ غير الكوفيين بالنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣaʿadan is a painful punishment that rises over and overpowers the one punished; a verbal noun used adjectivally.
rows.anchor: شاقا يعلو المعذب ويغلبه مصدر وصف به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mosques are devoted exclusively to God, so no one else may be worshipped in them.
rows.anchor: مختصة به. { فلا تدعوا مع الله أحدا } فلا تعبدوا فيها غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking an implied lām after “that” as the reason for the prohibition would erase the explanatory value of the fa.
rows.anchor: ومن جعل { أن } مقدرة باللام علة للنهي ألغى فائدة الفاء

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: “Mosques” may refer to the whole earth, since it was made a place of prayer for the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد ب { المسجد } الأرض كلها لأنها جعلت للنبي عليه الصلاة والسلام مسجدا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, it means the Sacred Mosque; the word may also mean places of prostration, with a prohibition on prostrating to anyone but God.
rows.anchor: وقيل المسجد الحرام لأنه قيل المساجد ومواضع السجود على أن المراد النهي عن السجود لغير الله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, the plural refers to the body's seven prostration limbs or to prostrations themselves.
rows.anchor: وآرابه السبعة أو السجدات على أنه جمع مسجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “servant of God” is the Prophet; calling him servant is humble self-reference and points to the quality that occasioned his standing.
rows.anchor: أي النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام وإنما ذكر بلفظ العبد للتواضع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To call upon God here means to worship Him.
rows.anchor: هو المقتضى لقيامه. { يدعوه } يعبده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The jinn nearly crowded around the Prophet, amazed at his worship and what they heard of his recitation.
rows.anchor: كاد الجن. { يكونون عليه لبدا } متراكمين من ازدحامهم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, humans and jinn nearly gathered against him to frustrate his mission.
rows.anchor: أو كاد الإنس والجن يكونون عليه مجتمعين لإبطال أمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Labad is a pile, like the matted mane of a lion.
rows.anchor: وهو جمع لبدة وهي ما تلبد بعضه على بعض كلبدة الأسد

rows.speaker: ابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads lubadan with ḍamma on the lām, a dialectal plural of lubda.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عامر «لبدا» بضم اللام جمع لبدة وهي لغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other readings are lubadan, a plural of lābid, and lubadan like ṣubaran, a plural of labūd.
rows.anchor: وقرىء «لبدا» كسجدا جمع لابد و «لبدا» كصبر جمع لبود

words: إنما أدعو ربي ولا أشرك به أحدا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worshipping and invoking God alone is neither novel nor a reason for amazement or united opposition.
rows.anchor: فليس ذلك ببدع ولا منكر يوجب تعجبكم أو إطباقكم على مقتي

rows.speaker: عاصم وحمزة
rows.claim: ʿĀṣim and Ḥamza read “قل” as a command to the Prophet, aligning it with what follows.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عاصم وحمزة «قل» على الأمر للنبي عليه الصلاة والسلام ليوافق ما بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage was revealed concerning al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra.
rows.anchor: نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waḥīdan may be circumstantial from the first-person pronoun: “leave me alone with him,” for God will suffice against him.
rows.anchor: حال من الياء أي ذرني وحدي معه فإني أكفيكه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it is circumstantial from the subject of “I created,” meaning God created him alone, with no partner.
rows.anchor: أو من التاء أي ومن خلقته وحدي لم يشركني في خلقه أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it refers to the omitted object: he was created alone, without wealth or children.
rows.anchor: أو من العائد المحذوف أي من خلقته فريدا لا مال له ولا ولد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word may derisively repeat his nickname, or mean he was alone in wickedness or illegitimacy.
rows.anchor: أو ذم فإنه كان ملقبا به فسماه الله به تهكما، أو إرادة أنه وحيد ولكن في الشرارة أو عن أبيه فإنه كان زنيما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His wealth was abundant or continually growing; it included crops, livestock, and trade.
rows.anchor: مبسوطا كثيرا أو ممدا بالنماء، وكان له الزرع والضرع والتجارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His sons were present with him in Mecca, so he enjoyed their company and they needed neither to travel for work nor be sent on errands.
rows.anchor: حضورا معه بمكة يتمتع بلقائهم لا يحتاجون إلى سفر لطلب المعاش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the sons were present at gatherings and assemblies, where their standing and respect mattered.
rows.anchor: أو في المحافل والأندية لوجاهتهم واعتبارهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: It is said al-Walīd had ten or more adult sons; three—Khālid, ʿUmāra, and Hishām—became Muslims.
rows.anchor: قيل كان له عشرة بنين أو أكثر كلهم رجال، فأسلم منهم ثلاثة خالد وعمارة وهشام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gave him broad leadership and prestige, so he was called the Fragrant Plant of Quraysh and al-Waḥīd; he had been deemed worthy of precedence.
rows.anchor: وبسطت له الرياسة والجاه العريض حتى لقب ريحانة قريش والوحيد أي باستحقاقه الرياسة والتقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His hope for further increase is far-fetched either because he has already received all that can be given or because his ingratitude and defiance make him undeserving.
rows.anchor: وهو استبعاد لطمعه أما لأنه لا مزيد على ما أوتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kallā rebukes his hope and, as a resumed explanation, grounds the rebuke in defiance of the signs that merited removal of grace and blocked further increase.
rows.anchor: فإنه ردع له عن الطمع وتعليل للردع على سبيل الاستئناف بمعاندة آيات المنعم المناسبة لإزالة النعمة المانعة عن الزيادة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: It is said that his wealth kept declining after this verse was revealed until he died.
rows.anchor: قيل: ما زال بعد نزول هذه الآية في نقصان ماله حتى هلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Suʿūd is a difficult, steep ascent, used as an image for the hardships that will overwhelm him.
rows.anchor: سأغشيه عقبة شاقة المصعد، وهو مثل لما يلقى من الشدائد

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet describes Suʿūd as a mountain of fire climbed for seventy autumns before the climber falls through it forever.
rows.anchor:
وعنه عليه الصلاة والسلام
" الصعود جبل من نار يصعد فيه سبعين خريفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated curse intensifies the expression; thumma marks the second instance as stronger, while its later use retains its ordinary sequential meaning.
rows.anchor: تكرير للمبالغة وثم للدلالة على أن الثانية أبلغ من الأولى وفيما بعد على أصلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He considered the Qurʾān repeatedly.
rows.anchor: أي في أمر القرآن مرة بعد أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He frowned because he could find no fault in the Qurʾān and did not know what to say, or because he looked at the Prophet and scowled at him.
rows.anchor: قطب وجهه لما لم يجد فيه مطعنا ولم يدر ما يقول، أو نظر إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Basara follows ʿabasa as an echoing expression.
rows.anchor: اتباع لعبس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He turned away from the truth or the Messenger and arrogantly refused to follow.
rows.anchor: عن الحق أو الرسول عليه الصلاة والسلام. { واستكبر } عن اتباعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He calls it magic that is transmitted or learned; the fa marks his blurting out the phrase as soon as it occurred to him.
rows.anchor: يروى ويتعلم، والفاء للدلالة على أنه لما خطرت هذه الكلمة بباله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that it is human speech confirms the previous claim, so it is not joined to it with a conjunction.
rows.anchor: كالتأكيد للجملة الأولى ولذلك لم يعطف عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording magnifies the dread of Saqar.
rows.anchor: تفخيم لشأنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question likewise magnifies Saqar's terrifying character.
rows.anchor: تفخيم لشأنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Fire neither leaves anything thrown into it nor spares it before destroying it; this explains its nature or describes Saqar circumstantially.
rows.anchor: بيان لذلك أو حال من سقر، والعامل فيها معنى التعظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lawwāḥa may mean that it blackens the upper skin, or that it is visible to people.
rows.anchor: أي مسودة لأعالي الجلد، أو لائحة للناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word is also read in the accusative as a specification.
rows.anchor: وقرئت بالنصب على الاختصاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nineteen are either angels or classes of angels in charge of the Fire.
rows.anchor: ملكا أو صنفا من الملائكة يلون أمرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One proposed rationale is that human perception and action go astray through twelve animal faculties and seven natural faculties.
rows.anchor: أن اختلال النفوس البشرية في النظر والعمل بسبب القوى الحيوانية الاثنتي عشرة والطيعية السبع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another rationale assigns angels or classes to six levels for unbelievers, with one further level for Muslim sinners, each class administering a fitting punishment.
rows.anchor: أو أن لجهنم سبع دركات ست منها لأصناف الكفار وكل صنف يعذب بترك الاعتقاد والإقرار، أو العمل أنواعا من العذاب تناسبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further rationale counts nineteen waking hours after subtracting the five hours spent in prayer from the day's twenty-four, with keepers overseeing punishments for those hours.
rows.anchor: أو أن الساعات أربع وعشرون خمسة منها مصروفة في الصلاة فيبقى تسعة عشر قد تصرف فيما يؤاخذ به بأنواع من العذاب يتولاها الزبانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading quiesces the ʿayn to avoid successive vowels in a single compound numeral.
rows.anchor: وقرىء { تسعة عشر } بسكون العين كراهة توالي حركات فيها هو كاسم واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “تسعة أعشر” is also read as a plural of ʿashīr, meaning nine groups, or as a plural of ʿashr, yielding ninety.
rows.anchor: و «تسعة أعشر» جمع عشير كيمين وأيمن، أي تسعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The keepers are angels so they differ in kind from the punished, will not pity them or comfort them, and are the strongest and most wrathful servants of God.
rows.anchor: ليخالفوا جنس المعذبين فلا يرقون لهم ولا يستروحون إليهم، ولأنهم أقوى الخلق بأسا وأشدهم غضبا لله

rows.speaker: أبو جهل
rows.claim: After hearing that nineteen guarded the Fire, Abū Jahl challenged Quraysh to see whether ten of them could overpower one guardian; the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: روي أن أبا جهل لما سمع عليها تسعة عشر قال لقريش

words: وما جعلنا عدتهم إلا فتنة للذين كفروا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The number nineteen tests unbelievers, provoking scorn, mockery, and disbelief that so few could punish most humans and jinn.
rows.anchor: وما جعلنا عددهم إلا العدد الذي اقتضى فتنتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intended act of making the number may be its announcement, which makes the following explanation of its purposes apt.
rows.anchor: ولعل المراد الجعل بالقول ليحسن تعليله بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People of the Book gain certainty about Muhammad's prophethood and the Qurʾān's truth because the number matches their scripture.
rows.anchor: أي في ذلك وهو تأكيد للاستيقان وزيادة الإيمان ونفي لما يعرض للمتيقن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers increase their faith through belief in the Qurʾān and by affirming the People of the Book's testimony to it.
rows.anchor: بالإيمان به وبتصديق أهل الكتاب به

words: ولا يرتاب الذين أوتوا الكتاب والمؤمنون
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The absence of doubt reinforces certainty and increased faith, removing doubts that might otherwise arise even in the certain.
rows.anchor: أي في ذلك وهو تأكيد للاستيقان وزيادة الإيمان ونفي لما يعرض للمتيقن حيثما عراه شبهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those with sickness in their hearts are people of doubt or hypocrisy; the verse predicts in Mecca what would occur in Medina after the migration.
rows.anchor: شك أو نفاق، فيكون إخبارا بمكة عما سيكون في المدينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbelievers here are those resolute in denial.
rows.anchor: الجازمون في التكذيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask what God intends by this strange number, treating it as an astonishing parable; some assumed it was a parable.
rows.anchor: أي شيء أراد بهذا العدد المستغرب استغراب المثل، وقيل لما استبعدوه حسبوا أنه مثل مضروب

words: كذلك يضل الله من يشاء ويهدي من يشاء
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this manner God misguides unbelievers and guides believers.
rows.anchor: مثل ذلك المذكور من الإضلال والهدى يضل الكافرين ويهدي المؤمنين

words: وما يعلم جنود ربك إلا هو
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only God knows His hosts as they truly are: no one else can enumerate possible beings, comprehend their realities and attributes, or grasp why each has its specific qualities and relations.
rows.anchor: إذ لا سبيل لأحد إلى حصر الممكنات والاطلاع على حقائقها وصفاتها وما يوجب اختصاص كل منها بما يخصه من كم وكيف واعتبار ونسبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “It” may refer to Saqar, the number of its keepers, or the sūra; each serves as a reminder to humanity.
rows.anchor: وما سقر أو عدة الخزنة أو السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The moon loses its light; it is also read in the passive.
rows.anchor: ذهب ضوؤه وقرىء على البناء للمفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun and moon are joined in loss of light or in rising from the west; the eclipse image can mean the moon's disappearance.
rows.anchor: في ذهاب الضوء أو الطلوع من المغرب، ولا ينافيه الخسوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For those who take the scene as a sign of death, the eclipse can mean loss of sight's light and the joining can mean the soul taking its senses with it, or reaching its source of rational light among the heavenly inhabitants.
rows.anchor: ولمن حمل ذلك أمارات الموت أن يفسر الخسوف بذهاب ضوء البصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb is masculine because it precedes its subject and gives precedence to the coordinated element.
rows.anchor: وتذكير الفعل لتقدمه وتغليب المعطوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human asks where escape is, expressing despair of finding it and wishing it existed.
rows.anchor: أي الفرار يقوله قول الآيس من وجدانه المتمني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A kasra reading makes al-mafir mean the place of flight.
rows.anchor: وقرىء بالكسر وهو المكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kallā rebukes the attempt to flee; there is no refuge.
rows.anchor: ردع عن طلب المفر. { لا وزر } لا ملجأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word “refuge” is a metaphor drawn from a mountain stronghold; its derivation relates to burden.
rows.anchor: مستعار من الحبل واشتقاقه من الوزر وهو الثقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The servants' final settling is with God alone, or the outcome of their affair is subject to His judgment.
rows.anchor: إليه وحده استقرار العباد، أو إلى حكمه استقرار أمرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, their place of rest depends on God's will: He admits whomever He wills to Paradise or Fire.
rows.anchor: أو إلى مشيئته موضع قرارهم يدخل من يشاء الجنة ومن يشاء النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person is clear evidence against himself because he witnesses his deeds; “seeing” is applied metaphorically to the evidence.
rows.anchor: حجة بينة على أعمالها لأنه شاهد بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the word means a seeing eye, so no further testimony is needed.
rows.anchor: أو عين بصيرة فلا يحتاج إلى الإنباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if he presents every possible excuse, maʿādhīr may be the plural of maʿdhār, meaning excuse.
rows.anchor: ولو جاء بكل ما يمكن أن يعتذر به جمع معذار وهو العذر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may instead be the irregular plural of maʿdhira, by analogy with manākīr from munkar; the author calls this analysis preferable but questions it.
rows.anchor: أو جمع معذرة على غير قياس كالمناكير في المنكر فإن قياسه معاذر وذلك أولى وفيه نظر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command addresses Muhammad and the pronoun refers to the Qurʾān.
rows.anchor: يا محمد، { به } بالقرآن. { لسانك }

words: لا تحرك به لسانك لتعجل به
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He should not move his tongue before revelation is complete, fearing the words might escape his memory.
rows.anchor: قبل أن يتم وحيه. { لتعجل به } لتأخذه على عجلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will gather the Qurʾān in the Prophet's chest and establish its recitation on his tongue; this explains the prohibition on haste.
rows.anchor: وإثبات قراءته في لسانك وهو تعليل للنهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The recitation is delivered through Gabriel to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: { فإذا قرأنه } بلسان جبريل عليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet should follow Gabriel's reading and repeat it until it is firmly established in his mind.
rows.anchor: قراءته وتكرر فيه حتى يرسخ في ذهنك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will explain whatever meanings of the Qurʾān are unclear.
rows.anchor: بيان ما أشكل عليك من معانيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is evidence that clarification may be delayed beyond the time of the initial address.
rows.anchor: وهو دليل على جواز تأخير البيان عن وقت الخطاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage reinforces the rebuke against haste: haste is blameworthy even in the most important matter and foundation of religion, and therefore all the more elsewhere; it may also recall an event during revelation.
rows.anchor: وهو اعتراض بما يؤكد التوبيخ على حب العجلة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, the speech addresses the person receiving his record: he stumbles in fear as he hurries to read it, so God promises to gather and read his deeds; he should acknowledge or reflect on the reading, then God explains it through requital.
rows.anchor: وقيل الخطاب مع الإنسان المذكور والمعنى أنه يؤتى كتابه فيتلجلج لسانه من سرعة قراءته خوفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The faces expect a calamity so severe it breaks the backbone.
rows.anchor: تتوقع أربابها. { أن يفعل بها فاقرة } داهية تكسر الفقار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebuke is against preferring worldly life over the afterlife.
rows.anchor: ردع عن إيثار الدنيا على الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The implied subject is the soul, indicated by the context, as it reaches the upper chest.
rows.anchor: إذا بلغت النفس أعالي الصدر وإضمارها من غير ذكر لدلالة الكلام عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A present companion asks who can perform an incantation to cure the dying person.
rows.anchor: وقال حاضر وصاحبها من يرقيه مما به من الرقية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the angels of death ask which angels—of mercy or punishment—will ascend with the soul.
rows.anchor: أو قال ملائكة الموت أيكم يرقى بروحه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dying person realizes that he is parting from worldly life and its beloved things.
rows.anchor: وظن المحتضر أن الذي نزل به فراق الدنيا ومحابها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His legs twist together, leaving him unable to move them.
rows.anchor: والتوت ساقه بساقه فلا يقدر على تحريكهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the phrase means the hardship of leaving this life joins the terror of the afterlife.
rows.anchor: أو شدة فراق الدنيا بشدة خوف الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person is driven to God and His judgment.
rows.anchor: سوقه إلى الله تعالى وحكمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He did not affirm what must be affirmed, or did not give zakāt from his wealth.
rows.anchor: ما يجب تصديقه، أو فلا صدق ماله أي فلا زكاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He did not perform the obligatory prayer; both clauses refer to the person mentioned in the question about whether humans will be left without purpose.
rows.anchor: ما فرض عليه والضمير فيهما للإنسان المذكور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He denied the truth and turned away from obedience.
rows.anchor: عن الطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He strutted in pride; the word may derive from stretching one's steps, originally y atamaṭṭaṭ, or from matt, “back,” referring to twisting it.
rows.anchor: فإن المتبختر يمد خطاه فيكون أصله يتمطط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Awlā laka may mean woe or that God has brought near what he dislikes, with an extra lām as in 27:72; it may also mean perdition, be a form of al-wayl by metathesis, or describe the final return to the Fire.
rows.anchor: ويل لك من الولي، وأصله أولاك الله ما تكرهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated warning returns to him again and again.
rows.anchor: أي يتكرر ذلك عليه مرة بعد أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sudā means left without duties or requital.
rows.anchor: مهملا لا يكلف ولا يجازى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question renews the denial of resurrection and argues for it: wisdom requires commands to do good and avoid evil, which entails requital; since this may not occur in this life, it must occur in the next.
rows.anchor: وهو يتضمن تكرير إنكاره للحشر والدلالة عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person began as a drop of semen that was emitted.
rows.anchor: ألم يك نطفة من منى يمنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He became a clot; God then created and proportioned him.
rows.anchor: ثم كان علقة فخلق فسوى } فقدره فعدله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made from him the two categories, male and female; this is another argument from origination for resurrection.
rows.anchor: للصنفين { الذكر والأنثى } وهو استدلال آخر بالإبداء على الإعادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The argument from creating the two sexes leads to the conclusion that God can revive the dead.
rows.anchor: ولذلك رتب عليه قوله: { أليس ذلك بقدر على أن يحيى الموتى }

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet would say “Glory be to You, yes indeed” when reciting this verse.
rows.anchor:
عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
" أنه كان إذا قرأها قال سبحانك بلى "

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report promises that the sūra and Gabriel will testify on Judgment Day that its reciter believed in the Prophet.
rows.anchor:
وعنه صلى الله عليه وسلم
" من قرأ سورة القيامة شهدت له أنا وجبريل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase has an unexpressed “it is said”; “this” points to the rewards just enumerated.
rows.anchor: على إضمار القول والإشارة إلى ما عد من ثوابهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their effort is appreciated by being rewarded and not wasted.
rows.anchor: مجازى عليه غير مضيع

words: إنا نحن نزلنا عليك القرآن تنزيلا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾān was sent down in stages for a wisdom that required gradual revelation.
rows.anchor: مفرقا منجما لحكمة اقتضته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the pronoun with inna emphasizes that the revelation is specifically God's act.
rows.anchor: وتكرير الضمير مع أن مزيد لاختصاص التنزيل به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is to endure the delay of victory over Mecca's unbelievers and others.
rows.anchor: بتأخير نصرك على كفار مكة وغيرهم

words: ولا تطع منهم آثما أو كفورا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning covers any sinner or persistent unbeliever who urges the Prophet toward sin or unbelief.
rows.anchor: أي كل واحد من مرتكب الإثم الداعي لك إليه ومن الغالي في الكفر الداعي لك إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aw shows the two types are equally and independently deserving of disobedience; the prohibition concerns what they invite him to do, since compliance in something neither sinful nor unbelieving is not forbidden.
rows.anchor: وأو للدلالة على أنهما سيان في استحقاق العصيان والاستقلال به والقسم باعتبار ما يدعونه إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following either person in an act that is neither sin nor unbelief is not prohibited; the command forbids yielding to their sinful or unbelieving demands.
rows.anchor: فإن مطاوعتهما فيما ليس بإثم ولا كفر غير محظور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command is to pray to God during part of the night, perhaps the Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ prayers; the temporal phrase comes first because night prayer entails greater effort and sincerity.
rows.anchor: وبعض الليل فصل له تعالى، ولعل المراد به صلاة المغرب والعشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He should perform night vigil for a substantial portion of the night.
rows.anchor: وتهجد له طائفة طويلة من الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Warāʾahum can mean what lies ahead of them or what they leave behind their backs.
rows.anchor: أمامهم أو خلف ظهورهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The day is severe, metaphorically “heavy” like a burdensome load; this explains the commands and prohibition above.
rows.anchor: وهو كالتعليل لما أمر به ونهى عنه
